USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

A partial agonist

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

Two compounds occupy the same receptor population. At saturating concentrations, compound A produces the full tissue response, while compound B produces only 40% of that response despite occupying available receptors. Which description best fits compound B?

  1. Irreversible enzyme inhibitor by definition
  2. Partial agonist
  3. Full agonist with identical efficacy
  4. Neutral antagonist with no activity
  5. Drug with necessarily zero receptor affinity
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Partial agonist

A partial agonist has lower intrinsic efficacy than a full agonist in the same system.

Understanding the options

Partial agonist
A partial agonist has lower intrinsic efficacy than a full agonist in the same system.
Full agonist with identical efficacy
Its maximal response is lower.
Neutral antagonist with no activity
B produces a positive response.
Drug with necessarily zero receptor affinity
It occupies receptors, indicating affinity.
Irreversible enzyme inhibitor by definition
The observations concern receptor agonism, not a specified enzyme mechanism.
